nodes.label: Native Host Simulation Decision (Option A locked, v1)
nodes.rationale: Option A chosen for v1 because goals (speed, breakpoints, DSP correctness) are exactly what native simulation does best; ISA emulation would fight every one of them. Known blind spot: verifies correctness not real-time CPU/RAM budget on the Seed.
nodes.norm_label: native host simulation decision (option a locked, v1)

nodes.label: VS Code Extension Decision (Q3 resolved)
nodes.rationale: VS Code extension chosen because the official Daisy C++ workflow already runs inside VS Code (build tasks + marus25 Cortex-Debug); reuses editor, DAP-based debug UI, terminal, and tasks. Standalone Tauri/Electron + Monaco was the rejected alternative.

nodes.label: Feedback Loop Shortening as Core Value
nodes.rationale: Core value is shortening the feedback loop, not emulating the Daisy Seed CPU. Desktop environment where Daisy effects compile, run, and are inspected as if deployed to hardware.
nodes.norm_label: feedback loop shortening as core value

nodes.label: A1 — Daisy Effects are Host-Portable C++
nodes.rationale: Verified: official examples and user effects (tremolo, equalizzatore) are bare-libDaisy + portable; no fixed-point/intrinsics/register code.
nodes.norm_label: a1 — daisy effects are host-portable c++

nodes.label: R1 — Native Sim Does Not Validate Real-Time CPU/RAM Budget
nodes.norm_label: r1 — native sim does not validate real-time cpu/ram budget

nodes.label: Out-of-Process Emulator Decision
nodes.rationale: Three locked decisions converge: VS Code extension runs in Node.js (cannot run native C++ audio loop in-process); DAP model requires a separate debuggee process; crash isolation requires process boundary. In-process only made sense for rejected Qt/C++ standalone alternative.

nodes.label: P1 — Standalone Executable (vs P2 hot-reload)
nodes.rationale: Each emulator build links effect+shim+runtime main() into one native executable; redeploy = kill & relaunch. Chosen over P2 (dlopen hot-reload) for simplicity, debuggability, and isolation; relaunch latency is within NFR-1.
